course_description: Fundamental principles of digital information assurance, applied cryptography (AES, RSA, SHA-256), network reconnaissance, packet analysis, web application security (OWASP), firewalls, intrusion detection systems (Snort), and incident response.

course_outcomes.co_description: Apply cryptographic algorithms including symmetric encryption, asymmetric ciphers, and hash functions.
Analyze network attack vectors, packet payloads, and port scans using Wireshark and Nmap.
Evaluate system vulnerabilities, attack surfaces, and risk exposure using industry security frameworks.
Configure intrusion detection systems (IDS) and firewall access control lists (ACLs) to block cyber threats.
Design an organizational cybersecurity defense architecture integrating zero-trust principles and incident response.

weekly_schedule.topic: Cybersecurity Foundations: CIA Triad, Threat Actors, and Defense-in-Depth
weekly_schedule.teaching_learning_activity: Interactive Lecture and Security Tooling Setup

lesson_outcomes.description: Define Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, and non-repudiation
Configure isolated virtualized security labs (Kali Linux / Wireshark)
Acknowledge legal frameworks, ethics, and computer misuse laws

weekly_schedule.topic: Classical Cryptography: Caesar, Vigenère, and Transposition Ciphers

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain substitution principles, cipher keys, and frequency distributions
Perform frequency analysis to crack monoalphabetic substitution ciphers
Appreciate historical cryptanalysis evolution

weekly_schedule.topic: Symmetric Cryptography: DES, AES, Block Cipher Modes (CBC vs GCM)

lesson_outcomes.description: Contrast symmetric block ciphers with stream ciphers
Encrypt and decrypt confidential files using Python cryptography and AES-GCM
Value cryptographic strength and proper initialization vectors

weekly_schedule.topic: Asymmetric Cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange, and ECC

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain prime factorization, trapdoor functions, and public/private keys
Generate RSA keypairs and exchange encrypted messages securely
Demonstrate meticulous care in safeguarding private keys

weekly_schedule.topic: Cryptographic Hashes and Message Integrity: SHA-256 and HMAC

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe avalanche effects, collision resistance, and preimage resistance
Implement file integrity monitoring tools using SHA-256 and HMAC
Uphold zero tolerance for unauthorized digital tampering

weekly_schedule.topic: Preliminary Examination: Applied Cryptography and Math Foundations Exam

lesson_outcomes.description: Recall cryptographic formulas, modular arithmetic, and cipher modes
Execute timed file encryption and key generation coding problems
Exhibit professionalism and academic honesty under timed assessment

weekly_schedule.topic: Digital Signatures, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and X.509 Certificates

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain digital signatures, Certificate Authorities (CAs), and CRLs
Generate self-signed SSL/TLS certificates and verify digital signatures
Value trust hierarchies and authentication infrastructures

weekly_schedule.topic: Network Reconnaissance: OSINT, Footprinting, and DNS Enumeration

lesson_outcomes.description: Differentiate passive reconnaissance from active network scanning
Execute open-source intelligence gathering and WHOIS/DNS analysis
Emphasize ethical boundaries during security reconnaissance

weekly_schedule.topic: Active Scanning: Port Scanning with Nmap and Banner Grabbing

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain TCP three-way handshakes, SYN stealth scans, and UDP scanning
Perform comprehensive Nmap scans to detect open ports and OS versions
Display discipline in scanning only authorized sandbox targets

weekly_schedule.topic: Packet Analysis: Sniffing Protocols, ARP Poisoning, and Wireshark

lesson_outcomes.description: Identify plaintext credential leaks in HTTP, FTP, and Telnet traffic
Capture and analyze malicious packet payloads using Wireshark filters
Respect privacy rights and adhere strictly to ethical sniffing mandates

weekly_schedule.topic: Web Application Attacks: SQL Injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

lesson_outcomes.description: Analyze reflected XSS scripts and SQL authentication bypass payloads
Identify vulnerable web parameters and remediate code vulnerabilities
Commit to defense-first security engineering

weekly_schedule.topic: Midterm Examination: Network Scanning and Vulnerability Audit Exam

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize reconnaissance data, packet capture analysis, and web attacks
Identify and audit network vulnerabilities under timed inspection
Demonstrate technical competence under formal assessment

weekly_schedule.topic: Authentication Protocols: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and Biometrics

lesson_outcomes.description: Contrast knowledge, ownership, and inherence authentication factors
Integrate Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) protocols in Python
Value multi-layered defenses in identity verification

weekly_schedule.topic: Endpoint Security: Malware Classification (Viruses, Trojans, Ransomware)

lesson_outcomes.description: Describe static versus dynamic malware behavioral analysis techniques
Analyze executable file hashes and inspect sandbox system calls safely
Maintain strict containment when inspecting suspicious artifacts

weekly_schedule.topic: Firewalls, Access Control Lists (ACL), and Network Segmentation

lesson_outcomes.description: Differentiate packet filtering, stateful inspection, and next-gen firewalls
Configure Linux iptables / UFW firewall rules blocking unauthorized ports
Appreciate defense-in-depth principles through segmentation

weekly_schedule.topic: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS): Snort and Suricata Rule Engineering

lesson_outcomes.description: Explain signature-based versus anomaly-based intrusion detection
Write Snort detection rules alerting on malicious ICMP and port scans
Strive for high true-positive detection without alert fatigue

weekly_schedule.topic: Incident Response, Computer Forensics, and Disaster Recovery Planning

lesson_outcomes.description: Outline the 6 phases of incident response (NIST SP 800-61)
Acquire volatile RAM artifacts and preserve forensic chain of custody
Demonstrate calm leadership during simulated security breaches

weekly_schedule.topic: Final Examination & Capstone Defense: Cybersecurity Defense Architecture

lesson_outcomes.description: Synthesize applied cryptography, network defense, IDS, and incident response
Defend an enterprise zero-trust security architecture before a panel
Exemplify Perpetualite leadership and professional presentation ethics
